content:
The image shows a corn stalk node/internode area. Key observations:
- The stalk is tan/straw-colored (dried/dead tissue)
- There are tiny black specks/structures embedded in the stalk rind
- The node area shows tan to brown discoloration
- The small black structures are embedded within the stalk tissue (not rubbing off)

This matches **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot**: "Small black structures embedded within the lower stalk rind, with tan to brown discoloration of macerated pith in lower nodes."

The tiny black pycnidia embedded in the stalk rind are the distinguishing feature of Diplodia stalk rot.
